method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); shared definitions, two regulative rules (ss 42(3), 52(6)) and the Part 7 table in a rules module, the questions in a seat module importing it; each regulative rule run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Coroners Act 2008 (Vic), Act No. 77/2008, Version No. 046 (incorporating amendments as at 1 November 2026), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/coroners-act-2008.txt (committed text sha256 e85ac7156282c99a6acb6be3e2979a7c4958a2a25146d3218e2ce0a37746deff), converted from the Word file saved by hand by the owner on 2026-11-06

seat: the family member of the person who died: the senior next of kin, another member of the immediate family, or another person with an interest in the death (who reported it, asked for an autopsy, inquest or re-opening, applied for the body, was notified of an exhumation, or was given leave as an interested party) (cor-seat.l4); the ss 42, 50 and 57 questions are asked by anyone the coroner calls on as a witness or for a document

scope: Focus: reportable deaths, investigations, inquests and findings, with the family's rights, time limits and appeals.
